pr_title: fix: use last item in value array in the case of duplicate columns (mssql)
pr_body:
<!--
  😀 Wonderful!  Thank you for opening a pull request for TypeORM.

### Description of change

Closes #7775

<!--
  Please be clear and concise what the change is intended to do,
  why this change is needed, and how you've verified that it
  corrects what you intended.

  In some cases it may be helpful to include the current behavior
  and the new behavior.

  If the change is related to an open issue, you can link it here.
  If you include `Fixes #0000` (replacing `0000` with the issue number)
  when this is merged it will automatically mark the issue as fixed and
  close it.
-->

The `mssql` driver, by default, returns an array when the resultset has duplicate columns. For example:

`SELECT 1 as id, 2 as id` would restult in `{id: [1, 2]}`

See https://github.com/tediousjs/node-mssql/issues/1384 upstream issue for more information and discussion. While I can understand the intent behind it, this is in contrast to how other drivers handle duplicate columns (in which they return, by default, the last column value). It seems that `mssql` is hesitant to introduce an option to automatically select for this behavior, citing data loss.

For TypeORM, tho, we need drivers that return data in similar fashion consistently. This change will look for any arrays that `mssql` returns, and then loop over the resultset and replace that property with the last value.

This is a fairly edge-case scenario - It's not normal for TypeORM to generate a query with duplicate columns, but it can happen (see test case entities for example), and this protects the mapper from returning odd results.

Please also see the issue in which this closes, #7775

pr_comments: It looks like this fix will leave the streamed results in the old format. Perhaps there needs to be a transform stream attached to the readable that normalises the streamed rows too?
We do not change driver output for the `query` method.

I remember I had to introduce some changes (not remember where, maybe just in test cases) after mssql version upgrade. But we do not change the output of the underlying driver. If driver returns it this way, there maybe a reason? I can say that I have problems with design decisions on absolutely every driver TypeORM currently supports. Please don't give me another problem.

I'm not too involved in TypeORM so, my opinion shouldn't hold too much weight, but I'll share it anyway.

@blitzmann raises some good points in the linked issue https://github.com/tediousjs/node-mssql/issues/1384. The mssql driver is returning duplicate column names in a way that is not typical of any other database driver at the moment (at least according to him). When there is a duplicate column name, the MSSQL driver is returning all the values for the duplicate column as an array rather than just returning the last value.

Whilst I have my views (as the maintainer of the MSSQL lib) about which is "best", my view of an ORM/framework like TypeORM is to homogenise the DB drivers so that swapping database drivers is completely™️ transparent. ie: the idiosyncrasies are dealt with at the ORM level, rather than by the consumer of the ORM. That would mean if some odd-ball DB driver comes along and returns data in a completely unrecognised way (like mssql *could* return rows as arrays instead of objects) then it's for the ORM to coerce this data into the form that the ORM and the ORM consumer expects.

In short, the contract is between the ORM and the ORM consumer, not between the ORM consumer and the DB driver. This change seems pretty sensible in the context of how all the other driver behave.
@pleerock just seeing if there's been any more thought given to this. I'm still of the opinion that this should be at the ORM level to massage the data into a format that TypeORM is expecting.

I feel like I have to close this PR. Because:

* we have mixed feelings on these changes
* no community interest in this issue other few people

Closing it for a better times.

issue_context.title: MSSQL: Duplicate columns names return as an array, breaking mapping
issue_context.body:
<!--

## Issue Description

I have the following query builder (will post entities below as well)

```
getRepository(Post).createQueryBuilder('Post')
        .andWhere('author.id = :p0')
        .setParameters({'p0': 1})
        .select('Post.id, Post.title, Post.text, Post.author'.split(',').map(i => i.trim()))
        .leftJoinAndSelect('Post.author', 'author', '1 = 1')
        .getMany()
```

This produces the following SQL, irrespective of the driver used:
```
SELECT "Post"."id"        AS "Post_id"
,      "Post"."title"     AS "Post_title"
,      "Post"."text"      AS "Post_text"
,      "author"."id"      AS "author_id"
,      "author"."name"    AS "author_name"
,      "Post"."author_id"
FROM      "posts"   "Post"  
LEFT JOIN "authors" "author" ON "author"."id"="Post"."author_id"
		AND (1 = 1)
WHERE "author"."id" = @0
```

When using the MSSQL driver, the results look like this:
```
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "title": "Ultricies Sem Ltd",
        "text": "quam. Curabitur vel lectus. Cum",
        "author": {
            "id": [
                1,
                1
            ],
            "name": "Ursula Manning"
        }
    },
    {
        "id": 6,
        "title": "Nunc Interdum Feugiat LLC",
        "text": "elit, pellentesque a, facilisis non, bibendum sed, est.",
        "author": {
            "id": [
                1,
                1
            ],
            "name": "Ursula Manning"
        }
    }
]
```

Please note that this seems to be due to the inclusion of `Post.author`. Since we're doing a `leftJoinAndSelect` on `author`, it's going to select all properties. Also selecting `Post.author` seems to confuse the system.

I'm not entirely sure if selecting the relation via  `Post.author` is supposed to be supported. Changing the select to `Post.id, Post.title, Post.text`  (note exclusion of `Post.author`) and the join to `leftJoin` produces a result that doesn't bring back any author data (as expected), but using (`Post.id, Post.title, Post.text, author`) (with inclusion of author) seems to bring back the entire author data (also as expected). So I'm not sure if the syntax `Post.author` is supported.

Regardless of the usage of `Post.author`, I still believe there's some funkiness with it. It's addition to the the select shouldn't cause doubling up of values, and there shouldn't be a difference to the results output that depends on which driver you're using. 

### Expected Behavior

<!--
  A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.
-->

I would not expect the id under author to be turned into a collection. It seems it does this because of how the results are interpreted (there's two `author_id` columns that return, which I assume TypeORM is taking and considering it a collection)

SQLite driver using the same query builder and producing the same query returns the data as expected:

```
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "title": "Ultricies Sem Ltd",
        "text": "quam. Curabitur vel lectus. Cum",
        "author": {
            "id": 1,
            "name": "Ursula Manning"
        }
    },
    {
        "id": 6,
        "title": "Nunc Interdum Feugiat LLC",
        "text": "elit, pellentesque a, facilisis non, bibendum sed, est.",
        "author": {
            "id": 1,
            "name": "Ursula Manning"
        }
    }
]
```


### Actual Behavior

<!--

  Please wrap any error messages or output in code tags, instead of images.
-->

See above in description

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--

Just a quick update: 
```
getRepository(Post).createQueryBuilder('Post')
        .andWhere('author.id = :p0')
        .setParameters({'p0': 1})
        .select('Post.id, Post.title, Post.text, author.id'.split(',').map(i => i.trim()))
        .leftJoinAndSelect('Post.author', 'author', '1 = 1')
        .getMany()
```

Again, it's a `leftJoinAndSelect`, so it should be bringing back all columns, which it does. But I'm also including one of the columns explicitly (`author.id`) in the select. Regardless of whether or not the `Post.author` syntax is / should be supported (I would love clarification on this), this syntax is definitely supported and still shows the issue of certain properties doubling up on MSSQL.

Also, it's not restricted to just the ID (or any other "special" column). I can put in `author.name` and it'll double up the name.

Again, SQLite driver doesn't exhibit this, and the SQL  query that is produced is the same regardless of which drivers, so it must be the processing of the data that is different

@imnotjames  I believe the driver label is incorrect, should be MSSQL. Unless the thought is that this really is a bug with SQLite instead, which just seems odd to me.

I haven't tested in other systems
You tagged it as sqlite so the script marked it as that.
Does anyone have an idea on where to begin to look into this issue? I might be able to poke around if someone gives me an idea.

I'm reopening this as it seems to not be related to the snake case naming strat (at least, not directly. Using the snake case naming strat can make this more likely to rear it's head tho)

The issue seems to stem from how `mssql` driver handles duplicate column names. By default, it groups them up into an array. This breaks TypeORM's mapping as it expects data to come back scalar.

It seems the [documentation](https://github.com/tediousjs/node-mssql#handling-duplicate-column-names) surrounding this is also incorrect on the mssql package side. Their docs note 
> the default behaviour of mssql will only return column metadata for the last column with that name.

Which is the same thing `sqlite` package is doing, however that doesn't seem to be the case and I can't seem to get it to do this.

I tried to use `arrayRowMode` just to see what would happen, by TypeORM straight up doesn't support it and throws errors (the QueryRunner would have to be updated to understand the new return result)

Example code using `mssql` driver
```
const sql = require("mssql")
;(async () => {
    await sql.connect({
        user: "sa",
        password: "Admin12345",
        database: "tempdb",
        server: "localhost",
        options: {
            trustServerCertificate: true, // change to true for local dev / self-signed certs
        },
    })
    const result = await sql.query`SELECT 1 as id, 2 as id`
    console.dir(result)
})()
```

I'm re-opening this issue in this repo in case we want to maybe try to massage the data coming back from `mssql` to account for the array, or if there's a default we should be implementing in TypeORM to avoid this issue. Because as it stands right now, the default implementation breaks the expected return result whatever column is duplicated. I'll be reaching out to that repo to determine what else can / should be done in this scenario

I have mixed feelings. Consistency is good, but underlying issue of duplicated column names looks iffy.
